skill.name: changelog-generator
skill.description: Generate changelogs from git history using conventional commits, semantic versioning, and Keep a Changelog formatting.
skill.summary: Create structured release notes from conventional commits and version history.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, sample links, template literals, and expected changelog file access. Confirmed issues involve shell command construction around git tag ranges and unquoted tag expansion in copied shell examples. Semantic review also found unescaped commit text and fragile GitHub output handling in generated release notes.

remediation.issue: Shell command strings include git refs.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFileSync or spawn with argument arrays for git commands. Validate refs with git check-ref-format before use.

remediation.issue: Shell examples expand tag names unquoted.
remediation.suggestion: Quote variables, reject unsafe tag names, and build revision ranges without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Generated Markdown includes raw commit text.
remediation.suggestion: Escape Markdown and HTML control characters in commit subjects and bodies before publishing release notes.

remediation.issue: GitHub output uses a fixed delimiter.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique delimiter or write release notes through a temporary file instead of fixed EOF markers.
Add dry-run, backup, or confirmation steps before writing release notes to an existing file.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Commit Text in Generated Changelogs
semantic_findings.description: The examples insert commit descriptions and breaking-change text into Markdown without escaping. A repository with malicious commit text could inject misleading links or HTML into generated release notes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly append commit descriptions and body-derived text to Markdown output. Legitimate rendering may sanitize HTML, but the examples do not escape or neutralize commit-controlled content.

semantic_findings.title: Fixed GitHub Output Delimiter for Release Notes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow writes commit-derived changelog text to GITHUB_OUTPUT using a fixed EOF delimiter. A changelog line equal to EOF could terminate the output block and inject additional workflow outputs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow builds CHANGELOG from git log output and writes it between fixed EOF markers. This is a known fragile pattern when content can contain the delimiter.

content.value_statement: Manual release notes take time and often miss important changes. This skill turns git commits into clear changelog sections with version guidance.
actual_capabilities: Groups conventional commit types into changelog sections.
Highlights breaking changes before other release notes.
Suggests semantic version bumps from commit history.
Formats output using Keep a Changelog conventions.
Includes example workflows for local scripts and GitHub releases.
limitations: Quality depends on clear and consistent commit messages.
Generated notes still need human review before release.
Repository-specific release rules may need manual adjustment.
Example automation can run git commands and write CHANGELOG.md.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Library Release
use_cases.description: Create user-facing notes from conventional commits before publishing a new package version.

use_cases.title: Summarize Sprint Changes
use_cases.description: Turn recent feature and fix commits into a readable internal change summary.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Notes
use_cases.description: Apply the same changelog format across services and repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner release notes from recent commits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog for the current repository using conventional commits. Group changes by type and highlight breaking changes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Since a Tag
prompt_templates.scenario: Release notes for a specific version range.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate release notes for changes since v1.2.0. Use Keep a Changelog sections and suggest the next semantic version.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Human review of generated release notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a changelog for version 2.0.0, then list entries that need manual review because they affect migration or security.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a changelog workflow for a monorepo with packages, scoped commits, breaking changes, and GitHub release notes.

output_examples.input: Commits include new login support, a payment bug fix, and one breaking API change.
output_examples.output: A changelog with breaking changes first, then Added and Fixed sections with concise user-facing entries.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for changes since v1.4.0 and wants a version recommendation.
output_examples.output: Release notes for that range plus a suggested minor, patch, or major version based on commit types.

output_examples.input: A team needs consistent notes for a GitHub release.
output_examples.output: A release summary organized by change type, with warnings for entries that need manual editing.

best_practices: Use conventional commits consistently before relying on automation.
Review generated entries for accuracy, security impact, and user value.
Validate tag names and escape commit text before publishing notes.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated release notes without human review.
Using unclear commit messages that hide user-visible changes.
Running copied automation in untrusted repositories without reviewing commands first.

faq.question: Does this skill create a full CHANGELOG.md file?
faq.answer: It can guide creation of a changelog and includes examples that write CHANGELOG.md.

faq.question: Does it require conventional commits?
faq.answer: It works best with conventional commits, but it can place unknown messages in an other changes section.

faq.question: Can it suggest semantic versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps breaking changes, features, and fixes to major, minor, and patch suggestions.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should generated notes be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review them for accuracy, sensitive details, and migration guidance before release.

faq.question: Does the skill access external services?
faq.answer: The skill text includes public documentation links and CI examples. The core examples focus on local git history.
